To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) global genetic ancestry predicts cognitive ability, (b) the association between global genetic ancestry and cognitive ability is partially explained by parental SES and (c) the association between ancestry and SES is partially explained by cognitive ability.
1) global ancestry predicts cognitive ability, even when SIRE is taken into account; 2) global ancestry also predicts SES, even when cognitive ability is taken into account.

(a) global ancestry is associated with cognitive ability in a manner that is independent of SIRE, (b) the relationship between global ancestry and parental SES is also independent of SIRE (and, therefore, is likely independent of SES), and (c) the relationship between genetic ancestry and cognitive ability is partially mediated by parental SES.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ultimate causes of cognitive ability differences among Americans.
the ultimate causes of group differences in cognition and SES in America.
the causes of cognitive differences between SIREs in the United States.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
genetic ancestry, SIRE, and SES each contribute to cognitive ability and that genetic ancestry and SES contribute to SIRE.
the genetic ancestry of an American child is associated with their cognitive ability and SES, independent of their SIRE.
genetic ancestry is associated with both cognitive ability and SES, independent of SIR, and that these associations are consistent with evolutionary-genetic predictions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
genetic ancestry is a predictor of cognitive ability, independent from SIRE, and that the relationship is not fully accounted for by SES.
the relationship between genetic ancestry and cognitive ability is not fully explained by SES, but that SES does mediate the relationship between ancestry and cognitive ability.
genetic ancestry is an independent predictor of cognitive ability and SES, and that the relationship with cognitive ability is partially mediated by SES.
The main takeaway from our work is that
genetic ancestry and cognitive ability are related, even after accounting for SIRE, SES, and the interactions between these factors.
the genetic ancestry of individuals can be an important predictor of cognitive ability and parental SES, even when controlling for SIRE.
genetic ancestry is a useful variable in understanding cognitive ability and SES in America.
